items.entity: Load patch location on the right edge for Fig. 7(a)
items.description: Sec. 3.3 and the Fig. 7 caption only say the two designs share 'the same loading condition'. Which of the 18 patch positions (Sec. 4.1 indexing: index k = element rows 2k-1 and 2k from the top) was used is shown only in the figure. Table 1 (FEM benchmarks) lists vf 0.3 and vf 0.5 together only at index 9; Fig. 9 shows index 8.
readings: Index 9: rows 17-18, patch spans 0.444-0.500 of the edge height from the top
Index 8: rows 15-16, patch spans 0.389-0.444 from the top (position drawn in Fig. 9)
Index 10: rows 19-20, patch spans 0.500-0.556 from the top
Index 1: rows 1-2, patch spans 0-0.056 from the top (top corner)
Index 18: rows 35-36, patch spans 0.944-1.0 from the top (bottom corner)
Index 2 (0.056-0.111) or 12 (0.611-0.667): these also appear with both vf 0.3 and 0.5 in Tables 2-3
Any other index k: patch from (2k-2)/36 to 2k/36 of the height from the top

items.entity: Uniform downward load on the 2x2-element patch
items.description: Sec. 4.1: 'a vertically downward uniformly distributed force is applied on a small area occupying 2x2 elements next to the right edge'. The text does not say how this area load becomes nodal forces (body force on the 4 elements, traction on the right-edge segment, or equal nodal loads). Sec. 3.1 only says the force is given to the network as a pixel-wise image channel.
readings: Uniform body force over the 2x2 elements in the two rightmost columns, with consistent Q4 loads on the 3x3 patch nodes (weights 1/16 at corners, 1/8 at mid-sides, 1/4 at the centre)
Equal vertical force on each of the 9 nodes of the patch
Uniform traction on the 2-element segment of the right edge: 3 edge nodes with weights 1/4, 1/2, 1/4
Equal force on the 3 right-edge nodes of the patch

items.description: Sec. 2.1 says only 'a vertical distributed load with a fixed magnitude'. Sec. 4.1 gives no value, and does not say whether it is a total force, a per-element value or a pressure.
readings: Total force 1 N
Total force 1 kN
Unit force per loaded element (4 units total)
Unit force per loaded node

items.entity: Physical size of the square domain (side length and out-of-plane thickness)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only that 'the square design domain is discretized into 36 by 36 uniform elements'. No side length, element size or thickness is given, although compliances are reported in J with E0 = 69 GPa.
readings: Unit element size (L = 36) and unit thickness (non-dimensional)
L = 36 mm (1 mm elements), t = 1 mm
L = 1 m, t = 1 m

items.description: Fig. 7 is in Sec. 3.3, which gives no discretization. The 36x36 grid is stated only later, in Sec. 4.1, for the cantilever benchmark. The paper also uses 64x64 for the metamaterial example. Because the filter radius is given in pixels (4 px), the resolution changes the result.
readings: 36x36 elements (Sec. 4.1 cantilever setup)
64x64 elements (the other grid size used in the paper)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only 'uniform elements/pixels'. The element formulation (e.g. bilinear Q4) and the integration rule are never stated.
readings: 4-node bilinear square element (Q4), full 2x2 Gauss integration
Q4 with reduced/selective integration
8-node quadratic element (Q8)

items.description: No passive solid or void regions are mentioned. Sec. 4.1 remarks that some NN designs 'don't even have materials in the region where the external load is imposed', which suggests the load patch can be designed, but this is never stated for the FEM benchmark.
readings: No passive elements (all 36x36 elements designable)
The 4 loaded elements fixed solid (rho = 1)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives E0 = 69 GPa and nu0 = 0.3 but never says plane stress or plane strain.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.description: Sec. 2, Eq. (1) describes Emin only as 'a small value assigned to void regions'; no number is given.
readings: Emin = 1e-9*E0
Emin = 1e-6*E0
Emin = 1e-3*E0

items.description: Sec. 2: 'p is the penalization parameter, usually p = 3'. The value actually used, and whether p is ramped up during the run, is not stated.
readings: p = 3 constant
p ramped from 1 to 3

items.entity: Projection combined with the sensitivity filter
items.description: Sec. 2: the Bendsoe-Sigmund sensitivity filter (r = 4 px) is used, and the Wang et al. (2011) projection 'can be used' with beta starting at 1 and eta = 0.5. That projection normally acts on a density-filtered field, so it is unclear what is projected, and whether projection was used at all for the cantilever designs in Fig. 7.
readings: Sensitivity filter r = 4 px plus tanh projection (eta = 0.5) applied directly to the design variables
Density filter r = 4 px followed by tanh projection (standard three-field scheme), no sensitivity filter
Sensitivity filter r = 4 px only, no projection

items.entity: Schedule for increasing the projection sharpness beta
items.description: Sec. 2: 'beta is initially set as 1 and enlarges gradually'. The increment rule, how often it is applied and the final beta are not given.
readings: beta doubled every 50 iterations up to 32
beta doubled every 25 iterations up to 64
beta increased by 1 every 10 iterations
beta doubled whenever max density change < 0.01, up to 16

items.entity: Which density field the V0 = 0.3 limit applies to
items.description: Eqs. (4)-(5) constrain the mean of 'the density of the i-th element'. If projection is on, it is unclear whether 0.3 applies to the raw design variables or to the projected physical densities.
readings: Mean of projected (physical) densities = 0.3
Mean of raw design variables = 0.3

items.description: Sec. 2 says densities are updated by 'the gradient descent method', and Eq. (5) adds a Lagrange/penalty term lambda*g0. Step size, move limit and how lambda is chosen or updated are not given, so neither the final volume nor the local optimum is fixed.
readings: Gradient descent on Eq. (5) with fixed lambda and fixed step (volume only approximately 0.3)
Gradient descent with lambda updated every iteration (augmented Lagrangian or bisection) to enforce mean density = 0.3
Standard optimality-criteria (OC) update (move limit 0.2, damping 0.5) with bisection on lambda
MMA with volume <= 0.3

items.description: The text never states the starting design.
readings: Uniform rho = 0.3 (= V0)
Uniform rho = 0.5
Uniform rho = 1.0

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only 'the average number of iterations in each design is 150'. The stopping rule, which also decides how far beta gets increased, is not given.
readings: Fixed 150 iterations
Stop when max density change < 0.01
Stop when relative compliance change < 1e-3 after beta reaches its maximum

items.description: Sec. 2.1, Eq. (3) calls c 'the strain energy' (1/2 U^T K U), but the garbled Eqs. (3)/(5) appear to write U^T K U, and the tables report 'Compliance/1e-3J'. This matters only when comparing values, e.g. with Table 1 at vf 0.3.
readings: c = F^T U = U^T K U
c = 1/2 U^T K U (strain energy)
